    Changelog

    tidygenclust (development version)

    • gt_clumppling() is now a native R and C++ port, with modifications, of clumppling 2.0.10 (Liu, Kopelman & Rosenberg 2024, by Xiran Liu), previously developed as the separate package rclump: it gives the same results as the python implementation (which the test suite checks against stored results), without Python, and is much faster. Its input is always a gt_admix object: Q files can be read with tidypopgen::read_q_files(), so the arguments input_path, input_format and extension are replaced by x. New arguments cd_res, test_comm, comm_min and comm_max expose further options of clumppling, and mode_stats gives the statistics of each mode. The example data are now gt_admix objects (inst/extdata/capeverde_admix.rds and chicken_admix.rds).
    • The conda environment is no longer needed by default, as the core functionality is native. tgc_tools_install() gains a tools argument to choose which optional tools to install (fastmixture and ADMIXTURE), and tgc_fastmixture_install() and tgc_admixture_install() add a tool to an existing environment. clumppling is no longer installed, and the package no longer warns at startup if the conda environment is missing.
    • New gt_radmix(): ancestry estimation with the ADMIXTURE method, using a modified version of the algorithm of OpenADMIXTURE (Ko et al. 2023), with much of the C++ (OpenMP) code ported from OpenADMIXTURE.jl. It was previously developed as the separate package openadmixturer, and named gt_openadmixture() during development; it was renamed because it differs from OpenADMIXTURE (it does not select ancestry informative markers, it adds cross-validation, and it changes some details of the algorithm). It estimates ancestry proportions directly from the backing files of gen_tibble objects (no Python or Julia needed), supports diploid and pseudohaploid data and missing genotypes, implements the cross-validation of ADMIXTURE (which is not part of OpenADMIXTURE), and returns gt_admix objects. Its results are checked against OpenADMIXTURE.jl and ADMIXTURE in the test suite.
    • Fixed the colours of the clusters in the plots of gt_clumppling objects with K >= 10: clusters were ordered as text (“1”, “10”, “2”, …), so the same aligned cluster was drawn in a different colour (and position) for different values of K.
    • On Windows, tgc_tools_install(), tgc_fastmixture_install() and tgc_admixture_install() explain that only the optional tools cannot be installed (they said that tidygenclust did not work on Windows); the rest of the package does not need conda.
    • gt_fastmixture() now starts from the SVD-based initialisation of fastmixture by default (random_init = FALSE), as the fastmixture program does: random starting values, the previous default, can take much longer to converge. The SVD-based initialisation needs all the loci to be polymorphic; the error for monomorphic loci now says so, and suggests random_init = TRUE.
    • gt_fastmixture() now uses the individuals and loci selected in a gen_tibble: it read the whole backing file, so a filtered gen_tibble failed, and a reordered one gave the rows of Q in the order of the backing file while id followed the gen_tibble.
    • gt_fastmixture(threads = ) now limits the number of threads (with the python package threadpoolctl, which tgc_fastmixture_install() now installs): the environment variables used before had no effect once R had started OpenMP, and they stayed set in the R session.
    • gt_clumppling() checks its options: a non-finite cd_res made community detection loop forever, and invalid logical options gave cryptic errors.
    • subset_gt_clumppling(k = ) selects the right values of K: it failed when k covered all of K_range, selected K = 20 to 29 together with K = 2 (and so on), could not select values of K with gaps (e.g. 17 and 19 in the chicken example), and silently returned an empty object for values of K that were not in K_range.
    • subset_gt_clumppling(indivs = ) checks that the individuals are between 1 and N, rather than silently returning rows of NA.
    • gt_radmix() with fix_p = TRUE can project fewer individuals than k (e.g. a single new sample) onto a reference panel.
    • gt_radmix() matches the rows of init_p to the loci by their names, when it has row names (as its P matrices do): a P with the loci in a different order was silently accepted, giving wrong results, and a P with additional loci was rejected.
    • gt_radmix(crossval = TRUE) no longer changes the estimates of the following runs when seed is not given.
    • tgc_tools_install(reset = TRUE) with some of the tools no longer removes the others: the tools that were installed in ctidygenclust are installed again, and on macOS resetting ADMIXTURE alone leaves ctidygenclust untouched.
    • Installing fastmixture no longer replaces the numpy pinned by the conda environment with the latest version from pypi.
    • On macOS, tgc_admixture_install() uses the conda binary of reticulate (rather than any conda on the PATH, which may be missing, e.g. in RStudio) and quotes the path of the yaml file.
    • On macOS, a single path given to tgc_tools_install(conda_yaml = ) is only used for ctidygenclust; it was also used to create the environment of ADMIXTURE.
    • Plots of gt_clumppling objects subset by individuals draw the group boundaries and labels (and the number of runs of each mode) in the right place.
    • The group argument of the plots of gt_clumppling objects can be a factor.
    • autoplot(type = "modes_within_k") checks that k is a single value of K_range: other values gave an empty plot that failed when printed.
    • autoplot(type = "modes") no longer warns for a gt_clumppling object with a single value of K.
    • The vignette and the documentation of autoplot() no longer say that the edges of the ‘modes’ plot are labelled with their cost: they are coloured by it.
    • The Newton update of Q in gt_radmix() stops cycling at vertex solutions, which made it up to about 20% slower near convergence (results are unchanged).
    • gt_radmix() checks all its arguments before fitting: fix_q = NA was taken as TRUE, rtol = NA silently prevented convergence, non-integer values of k, n_runs and n_folds were truncated, invalid max_iter, n_qn and n_cores gave a generic error, and invalid seeds were only detected after the first fits.
    • gt_radmix() on a gen_tibble grouped by more than one variable fails with a clear error before fitting, rather than after all the fits.
    • gt_fastmixture() checks its arguments before starting python, with error messages naming the right arguments, and a single seed (such as the default) can be used with n_runs > 1: it is incremented for each run.
    • gt_radmix(fix_q = TRUE) keeps Q exactly at its starting value (it moved by rounding errors).
    • gt_radmix() on a gen_tibble without individuals or loci gives an error, rather than crashing R.
    • On Intel Macs, fastmixture is compiled with the llvm installed by Homebrew (its location was hard-coded for Apple silicon).
    • The safety argument of gt_fastmixture() is deprecated: it was never passed on to fastmixture, which turns on its safety updates by itself when an update is unstable.
    • gt_fastmixture() checks that a grouped gen_tibble has a single grouping variable before running fastmixture (it failed after all the fits).

    tidygenclust 0.1.4

    • Updated clumppling to v2.0.10, which is now installed in the same conda environment as fastmixture (ctidygenclust); the separate cclumppling environment is no longer needed.

    tidygenclust 0.1.3

    • Fixed gt_fastmixture() wrapper for fastmixture 1.3.0: P matrices are now returned in the original locus order, and gen_tibble input is shuffled and normalised as in fastmixture, giving the same results as PLINK input.

    tidygenclust 0.1.2

    • Updated version of fastmixture to 1.3.0
    • Use pre-tested conda environments to avoid dependency hell.

    tidygenclust 0.1.1

    • Updated versions of fastmixture and clumppling

    tidygenclust 0.1.0

    • Initial public version
